title: The Irishman: Did Frank call Hoffa about the last meeting he would ever attend or not?

commenti.body:
No, I don't see any way to read it as he made the call.

I think a more interesting question is whether he could have if he wanted. Remember, Russell owns the hotel (see, for example, the kitchen scene where he comments on their decision to get the oil and he's making the salad).

My read has always been that Frank is being tested by Russell. He couldn't have made the call if he wanted, but if he had tried they wouldn't have sent him to kill Hoffa. This is why Chuckie is there too, he's the backup plan if they couldn't get Frank to play ball.

If Frank had tried to call, he wouldn't have been able to, they wouldn't have sent him, and in short order they'd have killed him too.

I mean, YMMV, but I don't see how you get there.

>A few details that stand out to me: obviously the fact that Frank the very next morning was flown out to Detroit from Port Clinton to disappear Hoffa indicates that he may have made the call and the bosses as a result made him do this. But if he made the call, why does Hoffa still show up to the setup meeting and to his death? Yet, if he didn't make the call, then what phone call was he referring to at the very end of the film in the scenes with the pastor?

This kind of Cinema Sins-ish nitpicking for plot holes is one of the most tedious aspects of online film discourse.
